title: Adaptive client cancel fanout with deferred tool confirmation and soft-timeout policy
author: Priya Rao
commit_list: feat(stream): implement cancel fanout and subscription mesh
feat(stream): deferred toolcall confirmation handshake + idempotency tokens
perf(stream): soft server timeouts and adaptive sampling to reduce false-aborts
test(stream): add regression tests for racey cancel+toolcall scenarios
docs: design notes for deferred confirmation and operator knobs
body:
Motivation: Client-initiated cancels and abrupt disconnects continue to be a leading source of toolcall double-execution and noisy aborts in high-concurrency streaming workloads. This PR introduces a controlled cancel fanout, a deferred tool confirmation protocol, and a server-side soft-timeout policy that together reduce churn and make the OpenAI compatibility adapter resilient to intermittent network dropouts.

What this changes (summary):
- cancel fanout mesh: when a cancel is received from a client we now propagate a compact cancel token to all in-flight workers and stream proxies but edge the action behind a short sampling/confirmation window to avoid preempting toolcalls that have just committed. The token is revocable by the session leader.
- deferred tool confirmation: tool-runner components now emit a confirm/commit event back into the session mediator before the final output is sent. The streaming adapter will not treat an incoming client cancel as definitive if there is a pending confirmation window for a toolcall id. This reduces duplicate tool invocations in the common case where the client dropped while awaiting side-effecting tool confirmation.
- soft-timeout policy: server defaults softened from hard 2s cancel deadlines to a 200-800ms adaptive sampling window based on recent client disconnect rate. This trades tiny latency increases for significantly fewer false-positive cancels. The window is configurable per-tenant.
- OpenAI adapter changes: the compatibility layer now understands the cancel token semantics and defers terminal 'stop' events where deferred tool confirmations are outstanding; function-call idempotency tokens are attached where applicable.
- Observability: new metrics and traces for cancel fanout decisions, tool confirmation latencies, and soft-timeout sampling rates. Added SLI instrumentation for false-abort rate.

Design notes:
- The fanout uses a small, stateless token (token: hex, seq, ttl) so proxies and workers do not require tight coordination. The session leader keeps canonical state and can issue an explicit revoke to force immediate aborts (used for admin/incident flows).
- Deferred confirmation uses two-phase commit style: tool-runner posts a precommit (idempotency token + tentative result) then a confirm. Only confirmed toolcalls are considered durable; unconfirmed results are garbage-collected after a configurable tombstone window.
- Soft-timeout sampling: server keeps a sliding window of disconnect samples and increases the defer window when disconnect rate spikes. This is bounded to avoid unbounded latency.

Checklist: 
- [x] Implementation of cancel token fanout and revoke mechanics
- [x] Deferred tool confirmation + idempotency token plumbing
- [x] OpenAI adapter integration and compatibility tests
- [x] Metrics/tracing and SLI calculation
- [x] Integration tests simulating noisy mobile disconnects
- [x] Docs/RFC and configuration knobs

Tests and CI: all unit and integration tests in ci/workflows/streaming-tests.yml pass in the PR run. Stress runs with the stream_simulator show a 68% reduction in duplicate toolcall occurrences on a 5% client-drop scenario and maintain tail latency within the SLA for 95th percentile.

Files changed (high level):
- pkg/stream/cancel_fanout.go: main fanout logic, token format, revoke path.
- pkg/stream/soft_timeout_policy.go: adaptive sampling implementation; config knobs exposed.
- pkg/runtime/toolcall/confirmation.go: precommit/confirm flow and GC path.
- pkg/openai/adapter/streaming_adapter.go: compatibility handling for deferred confirmations and attach idempotency tokens to function calls.
- docs/design/stream-lifecycle.md and docs/rfc/deferred-tool-confirmation.md: design rationale and operator guidance.
- SDK changes: minor client-side helpers to emit idempotency tokens and surface confirmation state.

Review conversation summary: 
- Asha: requested more explicit guarantees around the revoke path and what admin users can force; asked for an e2e test that simulates a revoke during an in-flight confirmation.
- Author (Priya): added an extra integration test (scripts/perf/stream_simulator.go scenario 7) and an explicit revoke handler in session_manager.go.
- Michael: flagged a potential race between the GC window and confirm arrival; suggested extending tombstone window when soft-timeout is active. Implemented as config override and documented tradeoffs.
- Diego: asked for additional metric labels to identify tenant-level false-abort signals; added tenant_id label to the SLI metric and a small dashboard patch in docs.
- Final approvals: Asha (approved), Michael (approved), Diego (approved).

CI summary: build: pass, unit-tests: pass, integration-tests: pass, stress-smoke: pass, lint: pass. GitHub actions run: successful.

Release notes (for changelog): 
- Adaptive cancel fanout: reduces duplicate tool executions on client disconnects.
- Deferred tool confirmation: avoids eager aborts of side-effecting tool calls.
- Soft-timeout policy: lowers false-abort rate under noisy network conditions.

Backward compatibility and migration notes: 
- Behavioral change: servers will defer some final cancels by up to the configured window; operators can tune or disable via internal flag `stream.defer_on_cancel`. Default is enabled.
- No API surface breaking changes for SDKs; SDKs may opt into idempotency token helpers to improve guarantees.

Rollout plan: staged rollout on Dedicated and Hosted: enable behind feature-flag for 10% of sessions for 48h, monitor SLI (false-abort-rate), then ramp to 100% if stable. Private installs: documented operator opt-in.

Acknowledgements: design reviewed with Runtime, Client SDK, and Observability teams.
discussion_summary: PR had targeted review comments on revoke semantics, GC race, and tenant-level metrics. Author implemented additional integration tests, extended tombstone config, and added tenant identifiers on SLI metrics. All reviewers approved after changes.
release_notes:
- Adaptive cancel fanout: reduces duplicate tool executions on client disconnects.
- Deferred tool confirmation: avoids eager aborts of side-effecting tool calls.
- Soft-timeout policy: lowers false-abort rate under noisy network conditions.
notes_for_operators: Default behavior: stream.defer_on_cancel = true. Tombstone window defaults to 30s; can be increased when soft-timeout sampler is enabled. Admin revoke command available via session manager admin API for immediate aborts.
perf_impact: Measured: ~68% reduction in duplicate tool invocations under simulated 5% disconnects; median latency +10-30ms depending on confirm window; no significant change in 99th percentile in perf runs.
